title: What a non-zero exit of a remote compiler run means
description: A remote rustc run that exits non-zero is the build's verdict when its stderr consists of ordinary compiler diagnostics about the crate's own code (a genuine compile error is never compiled twice). It is not the verdict when the failure looks environmental, that is when the other machine lacked something this machine has: the unit is then compiled once more here (reason `remote-failed-local-redo`, with the head of the remote stderr, so remote-only failures are visible and countable). `codes` are the diagnostic codes that name a missing input (reason `incomplete-inputs`); every `classes` entry is a named class of environmental failure with the patterns (regular expressions, matched against the whole of stderr) that identify it; `noDiagnostic` names the class of a failure whose stderr holds no error diagnostic of the compiler at all. The exit statuses of a shell that could not run the compiler or of a killed compiler are infrastructure (`signalAbove`, 126, 127).
